thread_a.role: UDP sendmsg increments per-socket IP ID

thread_b.role: concurrent UDP sendmsg increments same IP ID

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: rho = atomic([read(inet_id), write(inet_id += segs)]) from thread_a (the per-socket IP-ID increment must be an atomic read-modify-write)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@ip_select_ident_segs:542 (thread_b) = mutate(inet_id += segs) concurrent increment that interleaves thread_a's RMW region
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: UDP sendmsg is lockless (no socket lock on the datagram send path), and inet_id is a plain u16 incremented with a non-atomic +=; neither sender holds a shared lock and the RMW is not an atomic primitive, so nothing serializes the two RMW regions
emergent_bug.category_rationale: rho is atomic(region [read,write]) of a counter RMW broken by a concurrent interleaving increment -> lost-update atomicity violation (KCSAN labels it data-race generically, but rho's shape is an RMW region)

fix_maps_to: patch converts inet_id to atomic_t and uses atomic_add_return(segs, &inet_id) for non-TCP (lockless) senders -> makes the [read,write] region a single exclusive atomic RMW, establishing atomic(region); TCP keeps the increment under the already-held socket lock = serialize(sk socket lock)
recall_risk_notes: Clean atomicity violation: object is in the static surface, the fix is an explicit atomicity primitive (atomic_add_return), and rho's RMW shape is inferable for a shared counter. Risks: (1) self-race / same-entry MHP - both contexts are concurrent sendmmsg invocations on the same socket, so the design must admit a same-entry concurrent pair; (2) guarantee adjudication - both sides are lockless but the LLM may wrongly assume the socket lock protects the datagram send path and falsely reject; (3) the access is inlined from a static-inline header helper (ip_select_ident_segs), so site grounding must resolve into __ip_make_skb.
